articles.title: The Rook Board: Marshadow leads the first Top 32
articles.dek: A provisional cross-position board built from visible scouting bands and workouts, with Iron Bundle climbing and Stakataka forcing a serious fullback discussion.
articles.author: calvin-rook

body.text: Marshadow is my first evaluation. Gateon State’s corner brings an 85–99 visible scouting band, a 4.55 forty, a 48-inch vertical and a 6.10 cone. I can make a football case for investigating that combination after a week in which one receiver gained 376 yards. I cannot turn it into a promise that a rookie will immediately solve the problem.

This is a provisional evaluation board across positions, rather than a predicted draft order. I began with the strongest visible scouting bands, then adjusted for the workouts and the jobs I would investigate. That puts Iron Bundle fourth despite a lower band than several names below him. Stakataka remains second because 87–99 deserves attention, with the fullback workload made explicit before anybody commits a premium selection.

The thirty-two names are distinct prospects with persistent universities and identities. Two Sigilyph and two Throh entries represent separate players. The supplied evidence contains no college game statistics, prospect injury predictions or guaranteed final ratings. Club suggestions below identify evaluations worth doing; no team has made a commitment, and a future rookie cannot fill a current Week 14 absence.

prospects.name: Marshadow
prospects.analysis: The corner leads my board because the 85–99 band comes with a 4.55 forty,48-inch vertical and 6.10 cone. Gateon State has supplied an athlete worth investigating at a position that can change a passing matchup. Fortree should begin here after allowing 550 passing yards.
prospects.concern: The band is broad; the workout does not establish coverage technique.
prospects.projection: First defensive-back evaluation for Fortree and other clubs needing coverage.

prospects.name: Stakataka
prospects.analysis: Stakataka owns the strongest visible lower bound in this group,87, and adds 27 bench repetitions. I place the fullback second because the football assignment must justify the investment. A team that uses the role extensively can make a stronger case than one looking for an occasional substitute.
prospects.concern: A 5.23 forty and 7.28 cone invite questions about work in space.
prospects.projection: Premium fullback evaluation for a club with a defined blocking role.

prospects.name: Cryogonal
prospects.analysis: Icirrus University’s safety brings an 82–99 band and a 4.61 forty. The 39-inch vertical supports the athletic conversation without answering every coverage question. Mossdeep’s new safety absence is a reminder of the position’s value, though a future draft pick cannot repair this week’s lineup.
prospects.concern: The listed range does not guarantee an immediate starting standard.
prospects.projection: Early safety evaluation; compare coverage work before projecting a specific role.

prospects.name: Iron Bundle
prospects.analysis: I am moving Iron Bundle above several wider-band competitors because 4.53,47 inches and 5.96 through the cones is a remarkable outside-linebacker workout. Shalour Military Academy has given me a prospect I want to watch move through an actual football assignment. Mauville should investigate.
prospects.concern: The 69–97 scouting band leaves substantial uncertainty about current football quality.
prospects.projection: Athletic outside-linebacker priority, with role testing before commitment.

prospects.name: Dhelmise
prospects.analysis: Dhelmise combines an 80–99 band with 28 bench repetitions. That makes the tight end a compelling comparison for teams seeking a substantial blocking contribution alongside receiving work. I want the passing evaluation to explain how much the 5.06 forty matters within the intended routes.
prospects.concern: Level 5 means the current development stage deserves particular attention.
prospects.projection: Tight-end evaluation for teams seeking more than a detached receiver.

prospects.name: Comfey
prospects.analysis: Comfey’s 6.31 cone is the detail that keeps drawing me back. The Levincia safety also has a 40-inch vertical and a 77–99 band. I prefer this movement profile to the next safety’s slower sprint, while recognizing that neither drill supplies a coverage result.
prospects.concern: Twelve bench repetitions leave the strength comparison open.
prospects.projection: Safety shortlist for clubs needing a mobile option in space.

prospects.name: Sigilyph
prospects.analysis: Sonia University’s Sigilyph has a 77–99 band and a 42-inch vertical. I rank him behind Comfey because the 4.84 forty and 6.43 cone make the athletic comparison less persuasive. The band still warrants a serious evaluation rather than a dismissal based on one sprint.
prospects.concern: Ten bench repetitions and the slower forty need role-specific follow-up.
prospects.projection: Safety evaluation where the available coverage evidence supports the role.

prospects.name: Lapras
prospects.analysis: Lapras offers a 77–99 band with a 4.95 forty and 6.91 cone on the offensive line. Agate State’s prospect has enough movement to make a protection evaluation interesting. Fortree and Pewter should compare the actual blocking work rather than treating the position label as a completed answer.
prospects.concern: Seventeen bench repetitions are a comparison point, not proof of poor blocking.
prospects.projection: Offensive-line shortlist for teams reviewing pass protection.

prospects.name: Druddigon
prospects.analysis: Druddigon brings a 74–99 band and 23 bench repetitions to the fullback group. Po State’s prospect sits below Stakataka on my board but runs the faster forty at 5.11. A team can reasonably prefer that tradeoff if its fullback regularly works beyond the initial contact.
prospects.concern: The intended fullback workload determines how much value the club can realize.
prospects.projection: Alternative fullback evaluation for a broader movement assignment.

prospects.name: Eiscue
prospects.analysis: Paniola State’s Eiscue pairs a 71–99 band with nineteen bench repetitions. The 4.95 forty resembles Lapras’s, while the 6.96 cone is slightly slower. I want the blocking comparison to separate two prospects whose workouts alone do not establish a decisive football difference.
prospects.concern: A wide band leaves the current level of play unresolved.
prospects.projection: Offensive-line comparison with Lapras and the more developed candidates below.

prospects.name: Throh
prospects.analysis: Agate State’s Throh has the stronger visible band of the two Throh prospects here:71–99. Eighteen bench repetitions and a 5.05 forty describe the workout. Lavender should investigate the interior-linebacker group while keeping the two players’ identities and development stages separate.
prospects.concern: Level 16 and age 23 change the development discussion relative to the younger Throh.
prospects.projection: Interior-linebacker evaluation for a clearly defined defensive job.

prospects.name: Sigilyph
prospects.analysis: Petalburg University’s Sigilyph runs 4.73 and jumps 41 inches, with a 70–98 band. I prefer his sprint to the Sonia prospect’s, though the lower scouting floor keeps him below that earlier entry. Hoenn has a useful safety comparison here, and I would like both players evaluated in the same assignments.
prospects.concern: The two Sigilyph prospects are separate players; their reports must remain separate.
prospects.projection: Safety alternative for clubs comparing movement and scouting uncertainty.

prospects.name: Klawf
prospects.analysis: Klawf moves up from the raw band ordering because the 4.86 forty,21 bench repetitions and 6.83 cone make an attractive line workout. University of Sunyshore has supplied a prospect worth comparing with the higher-band linemen. The 65–93 range keeps the enthusiasm qualified.
prospects.concern: Athletic testing does not establish protection consistency.
prospects.projection: Offensive-line evaluation for teams seeking movement without ignoring strength.

prospects.name: Miltank
prospects.analysis: Miltank gives the halfback group a 65–93 band,22 bench repetitions and a 4.72 forty. The forty-inch vertical adds another useful athletic measure. Canalave’s new rushing absence illustrates why teams need options, although this draft evaluation concerns next season rather than an immediate replacement.
prospects.concern: The workout does not establish ball security or actual rushing efficiency.
prospects.projection: Halfback evaluation for clubs planning future rushing depth.

prospects.name: Qwilfish
prospects.analysis: Qwilfish’s 4.81 forty and 6.42 cone support an outside-linebacker evaluation alongside a 67–95 band. He is level 23, a different starting point from several prospects near him. I would ask a club to compare the current role directly before paying for an imagined development path.
prospects.concern: Seventeen bench repetitions alone cannot settle the contact assignment.
prospects.projection: Outside-linebacker alternative when the club values a more advanced current level.

prospects.name: Arctozolt
prospects.analysis: Lavender Forest’s Arctozolt brings a 67–95 band and a 4.87 forty at tight end. Twenty bench repetitions provide a useful companion to that movement. I prefer him for an exploratory receiving-and-blocking comparison rather than assigning a specialist role from the workout.
prospects.concern: Level 13 and the 7.18 cone leave several development and movement questions.
prospects.projection: Tight-end comparison for teams broadening the available receiving group.

prospects.name: Torkoal
prospects.analysis: Torkoal’s 68–96 band keeps the Cinnabar lineman in this group despite a 5.21 forty. Eighteen bench repetitions and a 7.24 cone do not make him the workout winner. They also do not replace the need to examine how he actually blocks.
prospects.concern: The movement profile needs careful matching to the intended line assignment.
prospects.projection: Line evaluation where blocking evidence outweighs sprint preference.

prospects.name: Shuckle
prospects.analysis: University of Mauville’s Shuckle has a 66–94 band, sixteen bench repetitions and a 5.19 forty. I want Wattson’s club to examine its own local prospect without mistaking familiarity for proof. The visible range earns an evaluation; the workout asks for more football evidence.
prospects.concern: The 28-inch vertical and 7.27 cone provide limited athletic separation.
prospects.projection: Developmental offensive-line comparison with a specific coaching plan.

prospects.name: Dracozolt
prospects.analysis: Dracozolt’s 4.82 forty and 6.85 cone are useful numbers for a defensive-end evaluation. The 64–92 band and level 7 make this an unfinished prospect. Turffield State has supplied enough movement to justify attention, particularly for teams seeking future pressure options.
prospects.concern: Current technique and readiness are not established by the workout.
prospects.projection: Defensive-end development candidate after direct football evaluation.

prospects.name: Granbull
prospects.analysis: Granbull enters with a 65–93 band at defensive tackle and a level 23 starting point. The 5.01 forty is respectable for the listed role. Fifteen bench repetitions make the strength comparison worth examining rather than assuming the species or position has already answered it.
prospects.concern: The available measures do not establish interior run-defense quality.
prospects.projection: Defensive-tackle comparison for clubs seeking a defined interior assignment.

prospects.name: Throh
prospects.analysis: The Mahogany Throh is 21 and level 11, with a 65–93 band and twenty bench repetitions. That differs materially from Agate State’s older, higher-band prospect. I would keep both on the same comparison sheet and make the development assumptions explicit.
prospects.concern: A younger age does not guarantee a better eventual player.
prospects.projection: Interior-linebacker development evaluation with the required time made clear.

prospects.name: Zangoose
prospects.analysis: Zangoose combines a 4.75 forty, forty-inch vertical and 63–91 band. Opelucid’s halfback is level 20, offering a different current stage from some earlier names. I want the rushing comparison with Miltank to use actual role work instead of declaring the sprint difference decisive.
prospects.concern: Neither ball security nor receiving reliability is supplied by these drills.
prospects.projection: Halfback alternative for a club seeking competition in the rushing group.

prospects.name: Bouffalant
prospects.analysis: Lilycove’s Bouffalant has twenty bench repetitions and a 4.96 forty alongside a 63–91 band. I like having an interior-linebacker prospect who invites both movement and contact questions. The next step is finding which defensive assignment makes those numbers useful.
prospects.concern: Level 13 means readiness remains a separate question from athletic appeal.
prospects.projection: Interior-linebacker evaluation for a team with a realistic development role.

prospects.name: Parasect
prospects.analysis: Parasect is level 24 with a 64–92 band and twenty bench repetitions. The 5.05 forty is faster than the two earlier fullbacks, though their bands are stronger. Cyllage’s prospect deserves a direct comparison when a club needs a useful current role rather than only a distant projection.
prospects.concern: The role must justify carrying and developing a fullback.
prospects.projection: Fullback alternative for teams comparing current stage and movement.

prospects.name: Pyukumuku
prospects.analysis: Ambrette’s Pyukumuku has a 64–92 band at interior linebacker, but the 5.23 forty and 27-inch vertical require a careful assignment. I would investigate the football evidence before making a broad claim about range. The prospect has a place on the board because the visible scouting remains promising.
prospects.concern: Level 8 and the slower workout create substantial readiness questions.
prospects.projection: Interior-linebacker project requiring a narrow, tested role.

prospects.name: Audino
prospects.analysis: Saffron Institute’s Audino is level 24 and has a 63–91 band. The 35-inch vertical is a useful distinction within this line group, alongside a 5.00 forty. A club comparing him with less developed prospects should separate present usefulness from assumptions about future improvement.
prospects.concern: Sixteen bench repetitions do not resolve the blocking-strength question.
prospects.projection: Offensive-line comparison where current development stage matters.

prospects.name: Tropius
prospects.analysis: Tropius supplies a 63–91 band, seventeen bench repetitions and a 5.06 forty. North Orre’s lineman is level 17. The profile gives a team enough to investigate without an obvious workout statistic demanding that it ignore the other candidates.
prospects.concern: The 7.10 cone leaves the movement comparison open.
prospects.projection: Offensive-line depth and development evaluation.

prospects.name: Klefki
prospects.analysis: Lavaridge’s Klefki has a 62–90 band, fifteen bench repetitions and a 39-inch vertical. The 4.86 forty is slower than several safeties above him. I still want a direct coverage comparison before turning that difference into a fixed ceiling on his football role.
prospects.concern: Level 9 and the broad range make readiness uncertain.
prospects.projection: Safety development candidate for a club able to provide a useful role.

prospects.name: Seviper
prospects.analysis: Seviper is the receiver on this provisional board, carrying a 62–90 band and nineteen bench repetitions. A 4.95 forty does not make the Celadon prospect an automatic deep threat. I would examine route work, contested opportunities and the actual receiving assignment before choosing the label.
prospects.concern: The combine does not supply catching or route-quality evidence.
prospects.projection: Receiver evaluation for a team seeking a specific complementary role.

prospects.name: Mawile
prospects.analysis: Mawile’s 62–90 band and level 14 place him among the outside-linebacker projects. The 4.98 forty and 6.89 cone are less spectacular than Iron Bundle’s. That makes the direct football comparison more necessary, especially before a team assumes the two can perform interchangeable jobs.
prospects.concern: Fourteen bench repetitions and the movement profile require role testing.
prospects.projection: Outside-linebacker development comparison with modest initial expectations.

prospects.name: Maractus
prospects.analysis: Last week’s leading kicker remains on my overall evaluation list. Maractus has a 65–93 band, but his 4.95 forty and thirteen bench repetitions still do not tell us which field goals he will make. Accumula State has earned a kicking workout invitation.
prospects.concern: No prospect accuracy chart or measured kicking-distance session is available.
prospects.projection: First specialist evaluation for clubs reviewing their kicking options.

prospects.name: Stunfisk
prospects.analysis: Stunfisk’s 63–91 band keeps a second kicker in the final places. Celadon Metropolitan’s prospect is level 8 and runs 5.07. I will rank the scouting promise here while refusing to turn a sprint into a claim about reliable range.
prospects.concern: Actual kicking consistency remains unmeasured in the supplied evidence.
prospects.projection: Specialist comparison after Maractus, with accuracy evaluated directly.

articles.title: Make the next possession count
articles.dek: Sunyshore and Rustboro won very different games by making the opponent pay for lost possessions. The finishing is the part worth copying.
articles.author: mara-voss

body.text: Karson Jones got seven touchdown passes from DeZhaun Watzon. Tyler Scarboro got one from Lombre and none from Porygon-Z. Both won because their teams made useful decisions after the defense returned the ball to them. That is the part of these games I want coaches to study before declaring that every answer requires a more spectacular offense.

Sunyshore gained 342 yards at Hearthome. The Haunts gained 335. The score was 53–17 because the Starseekers took the ball five times and repeatedly finished the possessions that followed. Serp Gardener intercepted a pass at 3:30 of the third quarter. Watzon hit Jolt Vick for a forty-two-yard touchdown on the next offensive play. Hearthome then fumbled, and Vick scored again thirty-four seconds after his previous touchdown began.

I like the aggression because the outcome supports it. The first throw attacked deep middle and finished immediately. The second touchdown came on third-and-nine through a short-right pass that Vick turned into thirty-five yards. Those were different routes to the same useful result. Jones did not need the offense to insist that every chance be completed in an identical way.

The next takeaway came from Vig Rothington, whose interception and return produced another opportunity. This time Sunyshore finished on fourth-and-two with a four-yard pass to EKTRIK RED. I am not going to flatten those three possessions into a generic claim that the quarterback was hot. The offense converted a first-down deep opportunity, a third-and-long completion and a fourth-down scoring chance. Each required a successful answer to a different situation.
Rustboro used a smaller advantage properly

Rustboro’s defense gave the offense a different task. The Stone led 14–3 after a scoreless third quarter. Huntail intercepted a deep-right pass with 4:58 remaining in the fourth, and Gorebyss made a forty-two-yard field goal at 3:47. That moved the lead to fourteen. Frosmoth’s later interception removed another Mauville possession.

A field goal is a useful outcome there. The Stone already had an eleven-point lead and needed to increase the visitor’s scoring burden while preserving the ball. I want Scarboro to recognize that value without pretending the same answer would have been sufficient in a game where Rustboro trailed. Situation determines the job. The job here was protecting a lead against an offense that had already gained yards without reaching the end zone.

Mauville threw for 239 yards. Rustboro’s two passers combined for 252. The difference in passing production was thirteen yards; the difference in interceptions was two. Rustboro’s offense retained its passing possessions, while its defense ended two of Mauville’s fourth-quarter opportunities. That is a much more useful explanation than pointing to the winning quarterback’s yardage total and stopping there.

The Stone also received a scoring pass from Lombre while Porygon-Z supplied most of the passing yards. I do not need to invent a private tactical explanation to value the result. The available players completed their assignments, and the offense finished two first-half touchdown drives. A team can distribute the work without making the scoring contribution less meaningful.
The next opponent may offer fewer gifts

Sunyshore hosts Canalave next, with the Bulwark newly missing Gabite for fourteen reported weeks. Rustboro visits Fortree. Both have reasons to expect opportunities, but neither should prepare on the assumption that the opponent will repeat last week’s turnovers. Jones needs the ordinary production from FLOAT SZN and Fera LaGatr when the field is longer. Scarboro needs the receiving work from Timmy, Gengar and Shieldon when an interception does not arrive at the helpful moment.

The important preparation is repeatable finishing. A defense can force a mistake without guaranteeing where the ball will land. An offense can practice the third down, the short-yardage decision and the protection that allow it to use the chance afterward. Sunyshore supplied an explosive example. Rustboro supplied a restrained one. I would keep both games in the review because the next score will tell the coach which version his team needs.

articles.title: Eterna has earned a lead worth protecting
articles.dek: The Thorns moved into first place by allowing Canalave six points. Their offense now has a chance to make the next month less demanding.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Eterna is 8–4, first in Sinnoh West and plus-twenty-seven in point differential. The Thorns reached that position by beating Canalave 14–6. I like a team that can make its best quality matter in a direct division game, and Eterna’s defense has given it a quality worth trusting across more than one result.

The Thorns have allowed 127 points in twelve games. Only Mossdeep has allowed fewer in their conference. That is enough evidence to treat the defense as the central reason for the record, without requiring every successful afternoon to become a claim that the offense has solved itself. Eterna has scored 154 points, fewer than several teams below it in the standings. The margin available to the defense remains modest.

I find that combination more interesting than a simple label about winning ugly. The players still have to make the stops when the score gives them little room. A 14–6 victory requires useful work late because one ordinary touchdown can change the feeling of the game. The Thorns have repeatedly operated under those conditions and now have a division lead to show for it.
First place changes the next conversation

Canalave is 7–5, one game behind. Eterna’s next trip is to Pastoria, which just scored three points at Veilstone. That matchup reasonably favors the Thorns’ strongest unit. It also gives the offense an opportunity to do more than supply the minimum total its defense might protect.

I would like to see Eterna make the next game easier for itself. That does not require an abrupt transformation into the league’s most adventurous passing team. It requires finishing an additional possession, avoiding the mistake that gives the opponent a short opportunity and retaining enough control that the defense can survive an occasional failed series.

There is a useful distinction between respecting a successful formula and asking it to tolerate every new burden. Eterna has earned its record through defense. It can continue to value that strength while demanding more support from the attack. Those requests belong in the same conversation because the defense’s repeated success makes the additional points more valuable, not less necessary.
The available defense has new work

Whiscash is newly listed out two weeks at outside linebacker. The designation comes after the Canalave game and matters before the trip to Pastoria. I would not turn the absence into a prediction of collapse. I would also resist treating a unit’s season total as permission to ignore which players will be available to produce the next stop.

Dewgong has a minor entry with zero weeks reported. That is different from a confirmed two-week absence, and it does not automatically establish the next workload. Eterna can prepare from the reported statuses without inventing a medical story around them. The football question is which available players can preserve the useful work and where the offense can reduce the amount being asked of them.

Pastoria has its own new absences in Sandygast and Watchog, each listed out one week. The Waves had won three straight before losing 10–3 at Veilstone. They have already demonstrated that a modest scoring afternoon can be enough when the defense keeps the opponent within reach. Eterna should recognize the resemblance and prepare to make its own possessions more productive.
The lead is an opportunity

The current fourth seed would put Eterna in the postseason as a division winner, but a current seed is not a clinch. Canalave remains close, and the remaining schedule will still determine the division and the bracket. I prefer to give the Thorns credit for what they have secured on the field so far: eight wins, a direct victory over the previous leader and a defense that has allowed barely more than ten points a game.

Those accomplishments give the offense room to improve from a favorable position. A team chasing from below often needs several other results before its progress changes the standings. Eterna can help itself immediately by winning at Pastoria. Another efficient defensive performance would be welcome. A little more scoring support would make the trip easier to complete and the division lead easier to defend.

articles.title: Blaine, start the comeback before halftime
articles.dek: Cinnabar’s twenty-nine unanswered points were excellent. Giving Viridian the first twenty-one was an unnecessary opening act.
articles.author: dorian-pike

body.text: Blaine, your team scored twenty-nine unanswered points and won a road game after trailing 21–0. I enjoyed the recovery. I would enjoy the next one considerably more if you removed the requirement to spend the first half looking finished.

Cinnabar beat Viridian 29–21, improved to 8–4 and kept the Kanto West lead. Gholdengo threw four touchdown passes, all after halftime. The Blaze turned a disastrous opening into a result that belongs among their most satisfying wins. They also supplied enough first-half mistakes to explain why a less sympathetic observer might decline to call the afternoon comfortable.

Viridian scored three second-quarter touchdowns. Dewott ran in from five and two yards, then a fumbled kickoff return gave the Titans another possession. Mr.Rime found Gabite for a ten-yard touchdown with twenty seconds left in the half. That is how Cinnabar arrived at the break needing three touchdowns before it could even discuss taking the lead.

I am willing to celebrate a comeback without granting the mistakes a ceremonial exemption from criticism. The Blaze lost two fumbles in the game. The first came after a reception, the second on the kickoff return. A team with ambitions beyond winning a division cannot keep treating possession as an optional detail between the more exciting parts.
Four touchdown passes changed the result

The response began after Gabite fumbled in the third quarter and Gyarados recovered. Gholdengo found Arcanine for a thirteen-yard touchdown at 4:18. He later found Frogadier for a one-yard score at 2:28. Cinnabar had reduced the deficit to nine by the end of the quarter, with both extra-point attempts unsuccessful.

The fourth-quarter touchdown to Arcanine came on fourth-and-three. Gholdengo threw deep right for sixteen yards at 5:38, and the successful extra point brought the Blaze within two. That is a play I want retained in every serious discussion of this team. Cinnabar needed to continue the possession and produced a touchdown instead. The quarterback and receiver completed the difficult part when the game still demanded it.

Thievul then intercepted Mr.Rime at 5:13 and returned the ball thirteen yards. Gholdengo found Frogadier for a four-yard touchdown at 4:03. Cinnabar had taken the lead, and the later field goal completed the twenty-nine-point second half. The defense had taken the ball back, and the offense had finally stopped leaving the most useful work unfinished.

Gholdengo’s final line was thirteen completions in twenty-three attempts for 125 yards and four touchdowns, with no interceptions. Viridian gained 314 total yards to Cinnabar’s 205. The Blaze won because they finished the opportunities that mattered and forced four turnovers, including two interceptions. That is a legitimate way to win a football game. It is also a warning against assuming the yardage total alone tells us who used the afternoon well.
The division lead needs a steadier version

Cinnabar has 243 points scored and 190 allowed, a plus-fifty-three differential. The record and the margin support a serious division contender. The 35–3 loss to Saffron the week before and the 21–0 deficit here support a demand for more consistency. I am keeping both sets of evidence because I would rather see Blaine build a team that can survive difficult opponents than win an argument by forgetting them.

The next trip is to Cerulean, which beat Fuchsia 13–7. The Tide have lost Seismitoad for a reported twelve weeks. Cinnabar has newly lost outside linebacker Octillery for five. Those absences change the available personnel, and the Blaze still need to make their own offense function before the score becomes a rescue operation.

I am picking Cinnabar 29–12. The passing game has just shown that it can finish several different kinds of scoring opportunities: thirteen yards, one yard, sixteen on fourth down and four after an interception. I expect that variety to matter against Cerulean. I also expect Blaine to notice that the league permits touchdown passes in the first half without a special application.

The Blaze have earned eight wins and a place at the front of their division. Their next useful improvement is a road game that begins with the same competence that rescued this one. Keep the four touchdown passes. Keep the defensive takeaways. Give the next opponent fewer free possessions before asking those strengths to do all the recovery work.

articles.title: Injury Report: Canalave loses Gabite before the Sunyshore trip
articles.dek: New long absences in Canalave, Olivine and Cerulean; Hobbes and Revis out two weeks; the full league status comparison.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Canalave will prepare for Sunyshore with Gabite newly listed out fourteen weeks. Olivine has lost Beedrill for a reported seventeen weeks before its trip to Blackthorn. Cerulean’s Seismitoad is out twelve weeks. Those are the longest new absences after Week 13, and each changes an offense facing an immediate need for more production.

The report below compares confirmed Week 13 availability with the previous issue. Recovery countdowns are separated from newly reported injuries. A zero-week counter or a cleared designation does not establish that a player appeared in the last game or will start the next one; the game reports establish appearances separately.
Canalave’s next rushing assignment changes

Gabite’s fourteen-week absence is a major development for a Bulwark attack that scored six points at Eterna and now visits a Sunyshore team coming off fifty-three. Canalave has relied on keeping games manageable. It now needs to identify the available rushing work while also producing more scoring support for the defense. The injury report confirms the absence; it does not confirm a new starting order.

Olivine’s seventeen-week Beedrill absence adds to a receiving group that has already worked through several injuries. Beedrill caught a fourteen-yard pass at Mt. Silver and fumbled on the play; the game archive does not establish that this was the injury moment. Gogoat’s previous one-week counter has reached zero, a different kind of update that should not be confused with confirmation of a return to a particular role. Blackthorn is the next opponent.

Cerulean won 13–7 over Fuchsia and now faces Cinnabar with Seismitoad out twelve weeks. The Tide need productive possessions against a Blaze offense that scored twenty-nine unanswered after halftime. Cinnabar has its own new absence: Octillery, an outside linebacker, is listed out five weeks. The two changes affect opposite sides of that matchup and should be assessed separately.
Lavender and Mossdeep add short absences

Hobbes is out two weeks after Lavender’s 23–14 win over Mahogany. He gained sixteen yards on three carries in that game, following 118 rushing yards at Cianwood. Machoke and Diggersby already contributed forty-five and thirty-seven rushing yards against the Frost, giving the Wails observed alternatives before Azalea visits. Mr. Clanky remains out one week and People Eater four. Machoke has a new minor entry with zero weeks reported; the next workload is still a team decision.

Mossdeep’s Luvrelle Revis is newly out two weeks before Petalburg visits. Revis recorded an interception and two forced fumbles at Fortree. His absence joins Ninjaskamara’s three remaining weeks, Richard Furman’s four and Marshall Flock’s two. Those three are recovery countdown changes from existing injuries. Petalburg has new minor entries for Meganium and Toedscruel, both reporting zero weeks, rather than new multiweek absences.

Dewford’s Vikavolt is newly out two weeks on the offensive line before the trip to Sootopolis. Eterna’s Whiscash, an outside linebacker, is out two before the Thorns visit Pastoria. The Waves have new one-week absences for fullback Sandygast and receiver Watchog. Mahogany’s Quilladin is listed out six weeks on the offensive line with division champion Mt. Silver visiting next.
Counters reaching zero

Sunyshore’s Myles Gabite, Saffron’s Emmitt Smoth, Blackthorn’s Ninjask, Viridian’s Sneasel, Vermilion’s Exploud, Olivine’s Gogoat, Lavaridge’s Stantler and Hearthome’s Sunflora have moved from one reported week to zero. These are recovery updates. They do not prove a game appearance or restore a starting job by themselves. In particular, Myles Gabite’s entry is the continuing recovery from the earlier injury, not a newly suffered minor injury.

Mt. Silver’s Garshawn Lynch has a new minor entry with zero weeks after rushing for 131 yards and three touchdowns. Rustboro’s Porygon-Z also has a zero-week minor entry associated with the new game, while My Way, Son remains out five weeks. The table preserves those distinctions instead of treating every injury field as the same kind of absence.

articles.title: Game of the Week: Petalburg takes its division lead to Mossdeep
articles.dek: Iron Valiant’s perfect passing afternoon meets Dram Marino’s explosive one, with the Eclipse missing Luvrelle Revis and the Pride trying to protect Hoenn West.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Petalburg brings a 9–3 record and the Hoenn West lead to Mossdeep. The Eclipse bring 12–0, a secured Hoenn East title and an offense that just produced 550 passing yards. This is the strongest meeting of division leaders on the Week 14 slate, with twenty-one combined wins and a useful contrast between Petalburg’s controlled 14–10 victory over Dewford and Mossdeep’s 79–13 win at Fortree.

I favor Mossdeep 34–20. The forecast is substantially closer than the Eclipse’s last result because Petalburg has earned a stronger assessment than Fortree. It still gives Mossdeep the edge through its passing and protection. The Pride can upset that judgment by making the long completions rare and using their own accurate passing to sustain possessions against a defense with a new absence.
Iron Valiant completed every attempt

Petalburg’s quarterback went fourteen-for-fourteen for 152 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions against Dewford. He took two sacks. The perfect completion line is the most useful starting point for Norman’s offense, although the fourteen total points show that completing every attempted pass does not automatically create a large scoring afternoon.

Venomoth caught five passes for ninety-one yards and a touchdown. Seviper caught four for twenty-six and the other score. Vikavolt added twenty-six on three catches. Petalburg therefore has established receiving production to bring into this matchup, with Venomoth accounting for the largest gains and Seviper providing a scoring finish from a shorter distance.

Both touchdowns against Dewford came on short-left passes. Venomoth scored from seven yards at 5:01 of the second quarter, and Seviper from five with twenty-two seconds left before halftime. The Pride did not score in the second half. Their defense preserved the 14–10 lead, but Mossdeep is likely to require more than two productive scoring possessions.

My question for Petalburg is how to preserve the accuracy while increasing the number of valuable chances. A controlled passing game can help avoid wasted downs and keep the defense from returning immediately. It must also produce enough distance and enough finishes to stay with an opponent whose last three games include 45,35 and 79 points.
Mossdeep offers several ways to extend a drive

Accel BeckhmJr’s 376 receiving yards at Fortree will dominate the preparation. The eight catches included gains of seventy-seven and seventy-five in the first half, then several more substantial completions after the break. Petalburg cannot treat those as ordinary outcomes it can comfortably concede while relying on a red-zone stop. Mossdeep repeatedly finished the remaining short distance when a long catch stopped just outside the end zone.

Gronkaludon is the second receiving problem. He caught eight of nine targets for ninety-five yards and a touchdown. Early against Fortree, his nine-yard catch on third-and-eight kept a scoring drive alive. That is the kind of conversion that matters when an opponent successfully prevents the largest gain. Mossdeep can still continue the possession through another target.

Ninjulio Jones caught all four of his targets for fifty-two yards and returned a kickoff for a touchdown. Shawn Mareman rushed for seventy-three yards and three scores, with another nineteen receiving yards. The Pride should prepare for those contributions rather than treating the game as a single confrontation with BeckhmJr. Successfully limiting the leading receiver is valuable; it does not automatically end the offense’s options.

Marino completed twenty-two of twenty-six for 550 yards and took no sacks. Petalburg’s first defensive objective is therefore to make the quarterback’s work less comfortable. That does not require declaring that a particular coverage or pressure call is certain to succeed. It requires enough disruption that Mossdeep must spend more plays completing each scoring possession and faces more opportunities to make a mistake.
The new absence is on defense

Luvrelle Revis is newly listed out two weeks. He intercepted a pass and forced two fumbles at Fortree, so his absence removes demonstrated recent production from the available secondary. Marshall Flock remains out two weeks. Petalburg has a clear reason to test the available defensive group through Iron Valiant and his receivers rather than assuming Mossdeep’s unbeaten record makes every matchup equally difficult.

Mossdeep also remains without Ninjaskamara for three reported weeks and Richard Furman for four. Mareman’s rushing work against Fortree is relevant evidence of how the available offense functioned, while Poury Holt added fourteen yards on four carries. The next workload should follow the actual lineup. The preview can identify successful contributors without presenting an unconfirmed assignment as settled.

Petalburg has minor injury entries for Meganium and Toedscruel, each reporting zero weeks. Those statuses differ from Mossdeep’s confirmed multiweek absences. They also do not guarantee the exact defensive roles or snap counts the Pride will use. Norman’s preparation should keep the available coverage options clear before confronting the league’s leading receiving production.
The rushing comparison is less comfortable for Petalburg

Oinkologne gained thirty-nine yards on thirteen carries against Dewford. Delcatty and Magneton added nine each. The lead runner averaged three yards per attempt, which did not prevent a win but left the passing game and defense responsible for much of the useful work. Petalburg would benefit from more dependable rushing gains here, particularly if it wants to keep the offense out of obvious passing situations.

Dewford’s Excadrill gained 116 yards on twenty carries against the Pride, and Gumshoos added forty on seven. Petalburg still allowed only ten points. That combination shows the defense’s ability to preserve a manageable score despite conceding rushing production. Mossdeep’s passing makes the next task more demanding: the Pride must protect against explosive throws while also preventing the available runners from finishing the short distances those throws create.

I would not ask Petalburg to reproduce Fortree’s game or assume Mossdeep will reproduce its exact efficiency. The relevant comparison is between the work each team has already shown. The Eclipse have several productive receiving targets and recent clean protection. The Pride have an accurate quarterback, a useful primary receiver and a defense that just won a close game. Petalburg needs those strengths to last through more scoring pressure than Dewford supplied.
What each result would change

Mossdeep has already secured its division and a playoff berth. Its remaining objectives include the conference’s top seed and first-round bye. Petalburg leads Hoenn West by two games over Rustboro and Dewford, both 7–5. A road win would strengthen that lead and give the Pride a direct result against the conference’s unbeaten team. A loss would leave the division chase dependent in part on what those pursuers do elsewhere.

Rustboro visits Fortree while Dewford travels to Sootopolis. Those games make Petalburg’s own result immediately relevant to the shape of the division. The Pride cannot control either outcome, but they can avoid giving both pursuers a chance to gain a full game by winning at Mossdeep. The schedule gives the league several connected results to follow without turning any unplayed game into a certainty.

The opening possessions should reveal how Petalburg intends to defend the field. If the Pride keep enough coverage deep to discourage BeckhmJr’s longest routes, Marino still has Jones and Gronkaludon available underneath. Petalburg then needs clean tackles that make those shorter completions consume time and additional snaps. If the Pride instead commit aggressively to pressure, the first responsibility is getting home before a receiver crosses the open space behind it. Either approach requires several consecutive successes against an offense that can change a score with one throw.

My checkable target for Petalburg is to hold Mossdeep below thirty and score at least three offensive touchdowns. That is a demanding combination, which is why the forecast favors the Eclipse. For Mossdeep, I want no more than two sacks allowed and at least three passing touchdowns. Those targets test the protection and finishing that most clearly supported the Fortree performance.

The final pick remains 34–20 for Mossdeep. I expect Petalburg to produce useful completions and keep the game considerably closer than the Eclipse’s latest outing. I also expect Marino’s protection, Gronkaludon’s intermediate work and BeckhmJr’s threat beyond the first tackle to create enough additional scoring opportunities. Norman’s best response is an offense that retains the ball and a defense that makes Mossdeep finish the difficult down before it can reach the easy yard.

articles.title: Two division champions, and five teams with a route to follow
articles.dek: Mt. Silver joins Mossdeep. Ellis Quill maps verified Week 14 clinching combinations, the remaining schedules and the injury concerns shaping the chase.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Mt. Silver has joined Mossdeep among the division champions. The Reds’ 45–0 victory over Olivine settled Johto West at 11–1, giving Connor McLarren’s team a playoff place and a home game in the opening round if it does not earn the bye. Mossdeep already owns Hoenn East and improved to 12–0 by beating Fortree 79–13. Both clubs can now concentrate on the conference lead while several pursuers try to secure their invitations.

Blackthorn has the simplest new berth route in Week 14: beat Olivine at home. Cinnabar and Sunyshore have verified division-clinching combinations involving help elsewhere, while Saffron and Petalburg can also secure playoff places through combinations below. These are guaranteed routes, including specified ties. The guide is a selection of verified sufficient combinations, not an exhaustive list of every tiebreak-dependent possibility. A result outside a displayed route requires a fresh standings check; it does not automatically mean a club remains unqualified.
Two division titles are secure

Mossdeep has twelve wins. Its nearest Hoenn East rival, Sootopolis, is 5–7 and can finish with ten. Mt. Silver has eleven wins; Olivine is 6–6 and can only tie that total by winning its final five. The Reds won both meetings with the Ironclads, 13–9 and 45–0, so that tie belongs to Mt. Silver. Azalea’s ceiling is ten wins and Cianwood’s is nine. The standings therefore show Y beside Mossdeep and Mt. Silver. No other current berth is mathematically secured.

Seven teams qualify in each conference: four division winners and three wild cards. Division winners occupy the first four seeds, and only the conference’s first seed receives a bye. A berth guarantees entry; a division title also protects a place among those first four. Neither conference’s bye can be secured this week. Even after a Mossdeep win, Sunyshore can still finish with fourteen victories while the Eclipse could remain on thirteen. Mt. Silver likewise has Saffron and Blackthorn close enough to prevent an immediate first-seed clinch.
Blackthorn: a win books the trip

body.text: The Dragons are 10–2 after beating Violet 30–17. They have already beaten Mt. Silver and remain close enough to influence the first-seed race, but their own division still includes Lavender at 7–5 and Violet at 6–6. Qualification would remove one uncertainty while leaving the title and seed to be settled. Olivine arrives with a new seventeen-week injury to fullback Beedrill, on top of an offense that scored zero against the Reds.

A Blackthorn tie also suffices if Pewter beats Vermilion, or if Cianwood beats Violet. Another verified tie route requires Azalea to beat Lavender and Cianwood to tie Violet. Those combinations reduce the number of rival non-division-winners that can finish ahead of the Dragons. Blackthorn can avoid depending on any of them by winning its own game.
Cinnabar and Sunyshore can secure their divisions

body.title: Cinnabar’s outright-record division route
body.description: All three conditions are required. A separate tie route is described below.

steps.label: Viridian does not win at Saffron

steps.label: Pewter does not win at Vermilion

body.text: Cinnabar can also clinch with a tie at Cerulean if Viridian and Pewter both lose. The Blaze would have eight wins and a tie; all three division rivals would be capped at eight wins. This is a useful consequence of the 29–21 comeback at Viridian. Blaine’s club needed four second-half touchdown passes to rescue that game, but the resulting eighth victory has placed a division title within immediate reach.

The injury report complicates the matchup without changing the arithmetic. Cinnabar outside linebacker Octillery is newly listed for five weeks, and Cerulean fullback Seismitoad for twelve. The Blaze then visit Blackthorn, host Mt. Silver, visit Celadon and finish at Pewter. Securing the title before those two leading Johto opponents would provide a considerable improvement in comfort, even though the remaining results would still affect seeding.

body.title: Sunyshore’s outright-record division routes
body.description: Either branch guarantees Sinnoh East; ties are distinguished from losses.

steps.text: Sunyshore beats Canalave AND Pastoria loses or ties against Eterna.

steps.label: OR tie plus help

steps.label: Sinnoh East secured

body.text: Sunyshore’s 53–17 win at Hearthome put the Starseekers at 9–3, with a 4–0 division record. Canalave now visits after losing 14–6 at Eterna and reporting a fourteen-week injury for Gabite. Karson Jones has a strong immediate opportunity, followed by Rustboro at home and Mossdeep away. The final two games are at Pastoria and Veilstone. Those direct division meetings preserve leverage for the chasing clubs if the title remains open.
Saffron can qualify while the division stays open

A Saffron win over Viridian secures a berth if Lavender fails to beat Azalea, or if Olivine fails to beat Blackthorn. Those are two separate help routes: either is sufficient. If Saffron ties, a Blackthorn win or a Cianwood win also guarantees qualification. More detailed verified combinations appear in the route table below. These claims secure a berth; they should not be read as an automatic Kanto East title.

Saffron’s defense has allowed three points in three games, and the Psi Corps remain 10–2. Vermilion is three wins behind at 7–5, but the clubs split their season series and the Volts still have five games left. The following two Saffron appointments—at Mt. Silver and home to Blackthorn—could rearrange the top of Kanto–Johto. Trent Scarboro’s team has already demonstrated that it can control an opponent for an afternoon. The coming stretch asks it to repeat that work against two of the conference’s best.
Petalburg needs a result at Mossdeep and help

One verified Petalburg route is a win at Mossdeep combined with Dewford beating or tying Sootopolis, Lavaridge beating or tying Mauville, and Eterna beating or tying Pastoria. All four conditions are required in that route. Petalburg can also qualify with a tie if Dewford, Lavaridge and Eterna all win. The combinations constrain the wild-card competition across Hoenn–Sinnoh; the berth is guaranteed even if the eventual Hoenn West title remains unsettled.

The Pride are 9–3 after beating Dewford 14–10. Iron Valiant completed all fourteen passes in that game, giving Petalburg an encouraging performance to carry into the week’s most difficult venue. Mossdeep will be without newly injured Luvrelle Revis, listed for two weeks. That is a relevant opening for the Pride’s passing game, although the Eclipse’s offense has just produced 550 passing yards of its own. My expectation remains that Mossdeep wins; the clinching route describes what Petalburg can secure if it earns a different result.

The chase continues beyond this week

Eterna’s 14–6 victory over Canalave gave the Thorns the Sinnoh West lead at 8–4. Eterna cannot clinch a berth in Week 14, even with a win at Pastoria. Its next games are home to Lavaridge, at Petalburg, at Oreburgh and home to Snowpoint. Canalave is only one win behind but faces Sunyshore, Mossdeep and Rustboro before its closing division games against Snowpoint and Oreburgh. Gabite’s new absence makes that demanding sequence more difficult.

Rustboro and Dewford also sit at 7–5. The Stone visit Fortree and Sunyshore, host Canalave, visit Mauville and finish at home against Dewford. The Breakers visit Sootopolis and Hearthome, host Oreburgh and Petalburg, then go to Rustboro. Their finale could settle several arguments at once, but both clubs first have opportunities to improve their position against teams below them. Dewford’s newly injured offensive lineman Vikavolt is listed for two weeks.

In Kanto–Johto, Lavender has won three straight and is 7–5. Azalea and Celadon visit next, followed by trips to Cerulean and Blackthorn and a home finale against Mahogany. Vermilion hosts Pewter, visits Olivine, hosts Mahogany and Fuchsia, and finishes at Cerulean. Olivine and Violet are 6–6 and have just lost ground. The next results will determine whether those clubs remain close enough for their late meetings to decide a wild-card place.

My first-seed choices remain Mossdeep and Mt. Silver, with Saffron and Blackthorn providing the strongest immediate challenge to the Reds. That is a forecast. The secured achievements are the two division titles, and the next guaranteed opportunities are the combinations above. With five games left for most contenders, there is ample room for the order of the remaining field to change.

articles.title: Week 14: Petalburg visits Mossdeep, and the chase gets crowded
articles.dek: Fourteen games, five writers and a week of direct opportunities for the teams trying to secure playoff places.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Petalburg at Mossdeep is my Game of the Week: two division leaders, twenty-one wins between them and a useful test of an unbeaten team with new defensive absences. Canalave at Sunyshore and Azalea at Lavender directly involve the chasing clubs. Celadon, Fuchsia, Oreburgh and Veilstone are on bye. Scores below are writer forecasts, with all five panelists retained for the weekly scorecard.

matchups.matchup: Viridian must keep its completions and its possessions
matchups.analysis: Saffron has allowed three points in three games. Viridian led Cinnabar 21–0 at halftime and lost 29–21 after four turnovers. The Titans can move the ball, but their next opponent has repeatedly punished unsuccessful possessions without needing a perfect offensive day. NeMarcus Tare just made four sacks, while HeeDee Lamb caught 126 yards. I favor the Psi Corps at home because Viridian needs both a cleaner possession game and sustained finishing against this defense.
matchups.awayKey: Finish with no more than one giveaway and at least 100 rushing yards.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Viridian below twenty points and turn at least two possessions into offensive touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Two struggling offenses get a direct comparison
matchups.analysis: Vermilion scored zero at Saffron; Pewter scored three against Celadon. The Volts still hold a current playoff position at 7–5, so this is a useful home opportunity rather than a game they can afford to dismiss. Chandelure threw no interceptions in the shutout but completed only twenty of forty-two. I expect the Volts to find enough short completions and defensive stops to win a small game. Pewter can change that forecast by making Vermilion chase more than two scores.
matchups.awayKey: Produce two touchdowns rather than relying on field goals.
matchups.homeKey: Reach twenty first downs or win with at least two touchdown drives.

matchups.matchup: Cinnabar needs its second half from the beginning
matchups.analysis: The Blaze scored twenty-nine unanswered at Viridian after trailing 21–0. Cerulean beat Fuchsia 13–7, a much quieter route to a useful win. Gholdengo threw four touchdowns in the comeback, and I expect that passing threat to create more than Cerulean allowed last week. The Tide can make this competitive by keeping the early score small and forcing Cinnabar to sustain possessions. My pick assumes the Blaze avoid supplying another opponent with a three-touchdown start. Cerulean also has a new twelve-week injury for fullback Seismitoad, while Cinnabar outside linebacker Octillery is listed for five weeks. Both clubs must absorb a fresh absence alongside their differing offensive form.
matchups.awayKey: Score in the first half and limit giveaways to one.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Cinnabar below twenty and score two offensive touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Lavender tests the next version of its backfield
matchups.analysis: The Wails have won three straight and now face another offensive absence: Hobbes is out two weeks. Mr. Clanky remains out one and People Eater four. Frosmoth threw two touchdowns against Mahogany; Machoke and Diggersby already supplied rushing work. Azalea comes off a bye at 5–7 and can directly hurt a team it is chasing. I prefer Lavender at home because Wailord and Luvdisc give the replacement passer established receiving production, while recognizing that two receiver fumbles kept the last game unnecessarily close.
matchups.awayKey: Win the turnover count and hold Lavender below twenty.
matchups.homeKey: Get at least ninety combined rushing yards and lose no receiver fumbles.

matchups.matchup: Mt. Silver brings the division title and a restored run game
matchups.analysis: The Reds clinched Johto West 45–0, with Garshawn Lynch rushing for 131 yards and three touchdowns. Mahogany converted two recovered fumbles into scores at Lavender but added nothing around them in a 23–14 loss. I expect Mt. Silver to control enough possessions through the run and Tic Thorpe’s efficient passing. The Frost need productive drives that do not begin with a gift from the opponent. Josh Alakazam remains out nine weeks; the Reds’ recent success belongs to their available group. Mahogany offensive lineman Quilladin has a new six-week injury, another concern against a Reds defense coming off a shutout.
matchups.awayKey: Rush for at least 130 yards and commit no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Add two sustained touchdown drives without relying on takeaways.

matchups.analysis: The Ironclads lost 45–0 at Mt. Silver and travel to a 10–2 Blackthorn team that just won 30–17 at Violet. Olivine completed twenty-one passes for 136 yards last week, then lost three possessions. It needs more distance from its successful throws before the turnovers are even considered. Hatterene’s attack has scored thirty in consecutive games. I favor the Dragons, with Olivine’s path resting on ball security and a much more productive rushing contribution. Olivine now lists fullback Beedrill for seventeen weeks. That adds a substantial absence to an offense coming off a shutout.
matchups.awayKey: Lose no fumbles and exceed 100 rushing yards.
matchups.homeKey: Score at least three offensive touchdowns and hold Olivine below twenty.

matchups.matchup: Violet gets a chance to stop the retreat
matchups.analysis: The Falcons have followed four straight wins with losses to Olivine and Blackthorn. Cianwood comes off a bye at 4–8 after an 18–17 defeat to Lavender. Both teams need a result that can be described without the phrase close enough. I give Violet a narrow home edge, with the passing game required to avoid the mistakes that spoiled the Olivine trip. The Crushers can win by restoring the rushing production that fell to forty-four Bibarel yards in their last game.
matchups.awayKey: Rush for 120 yards and keep the turnover margin level or better.
matchups.homeKey: Allow fewer than 120 rushing yards and commit no more than one interception.

matchups.matchup: Rustboro must make its own improvement travel
matchups.analysis: The Stone beat Mauville 17–3 after losing the first meeting 23–0. Their three takeaways mattered more than a modest passing-yard advantage. Fortree just allowed 79 points to Mossdeep, but I am not treating that score as a forecast for a different offense. Rustboro has productive available targets in Gibby Timmy, Gengar and Shieldon while My Way, Son remains out five weeks. I expect enough passing efficiency to win, provided the Stone avoid letting Floatzel’s running produce another long touchdown.
matchups.awayKey: Finish with two passing touchdowns and no more than one giveaway.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Rustboro below twenty and get at least 100 rushing yards.

matchups.matchup: Petalburg tests the unbeaten team with the division lead intact
matchups.analysis: Petalburg is 9–3 after 14–10 over Dewford. Mossdeep is 12–0 after 79–13 at Fortree, with Dram Marino throwing 550 yards and Accel BeckhmJr catching 376. I expect a much tighter game than that last score, but favor the Eclipse’s passing and protection. Luvrelle Revis is newly out two weeks; Ninjaskamara remains out three, Richard Furman four and Marshall Flock two. The Pride need to convert the available defensive changes into productive possessions while preventing repeated explosive throws.
matchups.awayKey: Hold Mossdeep below thirty and score at least three offensive touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Allow no more than two sacks and produce at least three passing touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Dewford has little room to waste a road chance
matchups.analysis: The Breakers are 7–5 after losing 14–10 at Petalburg. Sootopolis reached 5–7 by beating Lavaridge 14–10 and has a useful 3–1 division record. I favor Dewford narrowly because it needs a more complete offensive response and has remained competitive against strong opponents. The Surge have a real home chance, especially if the game stays within one possession. Their receiving group continues without Arbok, whose long absence changes the available targets. Dewford offensive lineman Vikavolt is newly listed for two weeks, complicating the protection and rushing work needed to recover from the Petalburg loss.
matchups.awayKey: Produce two offensive touchdowns and avoid a negative turnover margin.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Dewford below twenty and convert at least two scoring possessions into touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Mauville’s yards need to arrive with points
matchups.analysis: Togekiss threw 239 yards at Rustboro, but Mauville scored only three and lost three possessions. Lavaridge scored ten in a four-point defeat to Sootopolis. I expect a close game with more offensive production than either managed last week, and give the Dynamos the edge through their receivers. Mothim caught nine of ten targets at Rustboro. Preserving that efficiency while removing the late interceptions would make a substantial difference.
matchups.awayKey: Keep giveaways to one and score two passing touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Prevent completions of thirty yards or more and reach twenty points.

matchups.matchup: Eterna can make a small offense smaller
matchups.analysis: The Thorns beat Canalave 14–6 to take first place in Sinnoh West at 8–4. Pastoria’s three-game winning run ended 10–3 at Veilstone. Eterna has allowed 127 points all season, and I favor its defense against an attack that has already been operating with little scoring margin. The Waves can upset the pick by forcing the Thorns to win through sustained offensive production rather than a few useful possessions. Eterna outside linebacker Whiscash is newly listed for two weeks. Pastoria has one-week injuries for fullback Sandygast and receiver Watchog, reducing its available options for the immediate matchup.
matchups.awayKey: Hold Pastoria below seventeen and score two touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for at least 100 yards and avoid interceptions.

matchups.matchup: Canalave tries to keep Sunyshore’s possessions ordinary
matchups.analysis: Sunyshore scored 53 at Hearthome with seven Watzon touchdown passes and five takeaways. Canalave lost 14–6 at Eterna and now faces another road game against a division leader. I favor the Starseekers because LaGatr’s receiving volume and FLOAT SZN’s rushing provide productive options even if the turnovers do not repeat. The Bulwark need long, secure possessions and more than six points from them. This is a strong test of whether Sunyshore can finish drives without receiving repeated short opportunities. Canalave’s Gabite is newly listed for fourteen weeks. The long absence adds to the Bulwark’s challenge against a quarterback who just threw seven touchdown passes.
matchups.awayKey: Lose no more than one possession to a turnover and score two touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Get at least 100 rushing yards and hold Canalave below twenty.

matchups.matchup: Snowpoint brings consecutive wins to a turnover repair job
matchups.analysis: The Blizzard won 23–17 in overtime at Oreburgh, following 24–6 over Veilstone. Hearthome gave the ball away five times in a 53–17 defeat to Sunyshore. I favor Snowpoint narrowly because its recent results provide a more stable basis for trust. The Haunts gained 335 yards last week, so an upset can begin with retaining the useful plays they already produce. Fantina needs a game with one giveaway or fewer, rather than another passing total overwhelmed by lost possessions.
matchups.awayKey: Win the turnover margin and score at least two touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Limit giveaways to one and convert the passing yards into three touchdowns.

picks.reason: The Ironclads’136 passing yards on twenty-one completions leave too little gain per successful throw. Blackthorn should create more valuable possessions and establish a two-score advantage.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cianwood has had a bye to work while Violet has lost twice. The Crushers’ running game should make the Falcons defend a more patient afternoon than they want.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Violet can recover at home if it makes Cianwood throw beyond the comfortable rushing situations. The Falcons should create enough passing production of their own to finish narrowly ahead.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Crushers have been close to useful wins, including the one-point loss to Lavender. Their rested running group should make the difference in another game with little separation.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Violet’s four-game winning streak has been followed by two defeats. Cianwood should keep the ball on the ground and make the Falcons prove they can stop the retreat.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The home side has the narrower route to victory: contain Bibarel and avoid repeating the interceptions from Olivine. Violet should manage both well enough for a small win.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Rustboro’s defense just supplied three takeaways. Enough of that disruption should survive the trip, although Fortree should find this passing assignment less absurd than Mossdeep’s.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Timmy, Gengar and Shieldon all produced useful receiving yards against Mauville. Those available targets should give Rustboro enough answers without requiring a perfect defensive game.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Stone have tangible evidence of recovery after the Mossdeep loss. The clean passing and late defensive stops from the Mauville game should carry into another useful win.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Winona has an entire defense to embarrass into a response, and Floatzel still supplied a fifty-five-yard touchdown against Mossdeep. Fortree’s best rushing version should catch Rustboro looking ahead.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Rustboro retained its passing possessions and forced Mauville’s late mistakes. That combination should work against Fortree, provided the Stone prevent the long rushing play from becoming a recurring problem.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Petalburg has nine wins. Mossdeep has twelve and just gave one receiver 376 yards. The Pride should make this respectable without making me change the top of the rankings.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Marino took no sacks while throwing 550 yards. Petalburg has a much stronger overall record than Fortree, but Mossdeep’s protection and multiple receiving targets should keep producing scoring chances.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Pride have earned a serious visit between division leaders. I still favor Mossdeep’s established passing partnerships to provide the extra possessions that separate a competitive game from an upset.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: I would enjoy picking Norman here. Unfortunately, Marino’s passing and the Eclipse’s protection have supplied inconvenient evidence. Petalburg should compete and Mossdeep to win anyway.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The new Revis absence gives Petalburg something specific to test. Mossdeep’s passing efficiency and available rushing contribution should outweigh that opening over the full game.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Dewford stayed within four of Petalburg. The Breakers should bring enough offense to beat a Surge team that needed only fourteen in its latest win.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Sootopolis has just won a division road game and now gets home field. Its defense should keep Dewford’s scoring modest while the available offense supplies the deciding possession.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Surge have continued finding useful results despite the receiving absence. The home setting and a manageable scoring requirement should give them a narrow win.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Wallace has a 5–7 team that just won 14–10. Dewford just lost 14–10. The Surge should keep the favorable version of that exchange when the teams meet directly.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Breakers need a road response after Petalburg, and Two finished touchdown drives should be enough if their defense keeps Sootopolis’s passing gains contained.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Mauville turned 239 passing yards into three points. Lavaridge should keep the game close until another unsuccessful Dynamos possession gives the home side the useful margin.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Inferno can attack a Mauville team that just lost three possessions. I expect a close passing exchange, with Lavaridge’s home offense making one fewer costly mistake.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Mothim caught nine of ten targets at Rustboro. Mauville should preserve that reliable connection and find just enough better finishing to win a close road game.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Wattson has receivers producing real yardage, and Him should get more than three points from them this week. Lavaridge’s ten-point afternoon does not persuade me to pick the home side.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Dynamos have several productive receiving options. Improved ball security should turn that yardage into the extra scoring drive needed against Lavaridge.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Pastoria had won three straight before the Veilstone defeat. A home rebound that forces Eterna’s offense should supply more than its preferred small allowance.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Eterna held Canalave to six and has allowed 127 all season. That defense should make Pastoria’s three-point performance a problem the Waves cannot solve in one week.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Thorns have earned first place through repeated defensive work. I trust that consistency more than an immediate offensive transformation from a Pastoria team coming off three points.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Eterna keeps asking its defense to protect small totals. Crasher Wake should find enough rushing production at home to make the Thorns finally pay for a quiet offensive afternoon.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The matchup favors Eterna’s most dependable unit. The Thorns should limit Pastoria’s sustained drives and finish enough of their own opportunities to win comfortably.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Canalave scored six while Sunyshore scored fifty-three. A less extreme game than that comparison suggests, but the Starseekers have far more demonstrated ways should finish a possession.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: LaGatr’s ten catches and FLOAT SZN’s ninety-five rushing yards matter even without the five takeaways. Sunyshore should move the ball against Canalave through more than one dependable option.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Bulwark need their offense to support another difficult road assignment. Sunyshore’s receiving partnerships should produce enough points that a defensive-only answer cannot hold.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Karson Jones just received seven touchdown passes from Watzon. Byron just received six total points. The Starseekers should make Canalave bring a much more ambitious offensive explanation.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The turnover surge may not repeat, but Sunyshore’s rushing and short receiving production are still useful matchup evidence. Those ordinary gains should support another home win.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Snowpoint has consecutive wins and finally one away from home. The Blizzard should retain that slight advantage against a team still sorting through five giveaways.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Hearthome gained 335 yards against Sunyshore. Fewer lost possessions this week, allowing enough of that passing production should become points against Snowpoint.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Haunts’ final margin was much worse than their yardage production. A cleaner home game should reveal an offense capable of beating Snowpoint, even after the Blizzard’s two wins.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Fantina has five turnovers to remove from the next performance. The Haunts should keep the useful passing and deliver a much louder response at home.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Snowpoint’s consecutive victories provide the steadier recent evidence. The Blizzard should protect enough possessions to finish a close game ahead of Hearthome.
